A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Pedrotti, Maas and Mondelli. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports original simulations measuring Wasserstein errors for an asymmetric Gaussian mixture, two moons and a rescaled Swiss roll.

after.justification: Figure 1 retains the original simulation results for the Gaussian mixture, two moons and rescaled Swiss roll.

M1.justification: The initial inexact Langevin correction, reverse ODE/SDE procedures, discretizations and score truncation in Equation (4.5) are unchanged. The revised accuracy requirement in Theorem 4.2 changes the analysis, without changing the algorithm or training loss.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic sampling scenarios: an asymmetric mixture of two Gaussians, two moons and a rescaled Swiss roll. No additional coverage appears in the appendices.

E2.justification: Figure 1 continues to show two Wasserstein errors of the proposed procedure as correction time varies. No competing sampler is added or removed from an empirical comparison; the expanded prior-work discussion adds no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported simulations retain fixed T1, variable T2, Wasserstein evaluation of both stages and use of the untruncated score estimator. No evaluation setting or procedure is revised.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same analysis of sensitivity to the Langevin running time T2 on all three distributions. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 1 and its accompanying reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds run counts, seed specifications, explanations of uncertainty or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The simulation plots are identical, including both Wasserstein-error curves for each distribution. The finding that both errors decrease as T2 increases is retained, with no added or removed empirical results.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 relaxes Equation (4.7) from b(T1) <= epsilon^(2+36 beta delta^2)/(550 beta) to epsilon^(1+36 beta delta^2)/(34 beta). Former Lemma A.6 becomes Lemma A.4, replacing the conditional square-root estimate with E[exp(F)] <= 1 + exp(M)E[F], and Appendix C updates the proof accordingly. This is a targeted quantitative refinement; the Wasserstein and total-variation bounds themselves remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: convergence with a fixed finite perturbation time, mild distributional assumptions, logarithmic dependence and control through the L2 score loss. Added emphasis on training cost and stability restates existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of the roles of T1, T2 and early stopping, the interpretation of score truncation as technical, and the applicability qualifications are retained. The expanded introduction repeats explanations already present elsewhere in v2.

D1.justification: No implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware information or code/data access instructions are added or revised. The new notation table summarizes previously defined quantities without supplying new reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Lee, Lu and Tan's 2023 work on general data distributions and explicitly credits their already-cited 2022 work with earlier predictor-corrector bounds, distinguishing its log-Sobolev assumptions and dependence. The Yang–Wibisono reference receives a title/publication update rather than representing an additional comparison.

P1.justification: Section 5.2's proof moves into Appendix D, with corresponding proposition and lemma renumbering. Appendix A consolidates existing lemmas and adds a notation subsection. Local prose edits clarify training cost and correct the Figure 2 discussion from red to purple.

P2.justification: Appendix A gains an unnumbered notation table, and the proof relocation changes document layout. Figures 1 and 2 themselves remain identical, with their captions retained.

improvement.justification: Theorem 4.2 obtains the same stronger-loss guarantee under a weaker L2-error condition, supported by a simpler exponential-moment estimate and revised Appendix C proof. The notation table and more precise prior-work attribution also improve clarity. These provide a limited improvement in theoretical precision and readability while preserving the algorithm and empirical evidence.
